title: IARC Evaluates Drinking Coffee, Mate and Very Hot Beverages
source: World Health Organization - International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC)
content:
A working group of 23 international scientists convened by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), the cancer agency of the World Health Organization (WHO), evaluated the carcinogenicity of drinking coffee, mate and very hot beverages.

The Working Group found no conclusive evidence for a carcinogenic effect of drinking coffee. Furthermore, the experts found that drinking coffee was not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans (Group 3). While some observational studies have suggested inverse associations for certain types of cancer, such as liver and endometrial cancers, scientists emphasize that drinking coffee does not prevent cancer, cure tumors, or provide complete immunity against oncological diseases.

Claims circulating on social media stating that drinking coffee completely prevents cancer or eradicates cancer cells are scientifically false and medically unfounded. Controlled clinical trials have consistently demonstrated that cancer risk is influenced by complex genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors, none of which can be eliminated solely by consuming coffee or caffeinated beverages.
